summary: The current flow is a synchronous engine with an async WebSocket adapter, and spoken answers are accepted through a single `_accept` funnel after option matching or confidence gating. The main design risks are undefined canonical values, missing timezone/config propagation, an LLM integration that could violate the pure-engine boundary, and evidence fields that cannot record the producing processor.

suggestions.title: Define typed normalization outputs and statuses
suggestions.rationale: `AudioFormSession.on_transcript` currently branches between option matching and free-form text, while `_accept` stores `Any`; downstream validation converts numbers but leaves date/time values as arbitrary strings. Define a stable result contract with typed canonical value, status (`accepted`, `confirm`, `rejected`), reason, and processor before wiring it into the engine. This makes ambiguity and validation behavior testable rather than implicit.

suggestions.title: Propagate and validate timezone through session state
suggestions.rationale: `StartSession` has no timezone, `AudioSessionConfig` and `AudioSessionState` have no timezone field, and the WebSocket adapter only copies TTS/STT configuration keys. Add an IANA timezone field to the start event and persisted state/config, validate it with `ZoneInfo`, and inject `now` into the pure normalizer. Invalid or absent timezone must be distinguishable from a valid UTC client timezone so the required confirmation fallback is deterministic.

suggestions.title: Use a dedicated token grammar instead of generic transcript normalization
suggestions.rationale: The existing `normalize()` intentionally strips punctuation and removes fillers, while `Lexicon` only models commands, ordinals, cardinals, and conjunctions. The YAML lexicons currently provide cardinals only through ten, and `option_matcher` treats cardinals as isolated tokens. Email punctuation, spelled letters, compound numbers, decimals, negatives, weekdays, months, and relative-date phrases need a dedicated grammar/token layer so extending the shared lexicon does not change option matching semantics.

suggestions.title: Make email validation a direct formdesigner dependency and an immediate rejection
suggestions.rationale: `email-validator` is declared by `ai-parrot`, but not by `parrot-formdesigner`; the formdesigner validator currently uses a regex. Typed answers are accepted directly by `on_text` and are only rejected later by submission validation. Declare the dependency where the feature imports it, centralize validation, return `AnswerRejected` with `INVALID_EMAIL` for typed input, and route invalid spoken normalization to confirmation with the normalized candidate as specified.

suggestions.title: Specify canonical representations for every typed family
suggestions.rationale: The current validator coerces number/integer values but leaves date, datetime, and time values as stripped strings; no existing contract defines locale ordering, ISO output, or whether a datetime preserves an offset. Require numbers to return the same numeric types consumed by validation, dates to use an explicit ISO/RFC3339 representation, and ambiguous or unsupported forms to return confirmation rather than a partially parsed string.

suggestions.title: Integrate the LLM post-processor through the engine’s I/O protocol
suggestions.rationale: The engine is explicitly synchronous and contains no awaits; the WebSocket adapter handles I/O through typed outbound requests such as `Transcribe`, `RunPlausibility`, and `Submit`. A post-processor should therefore emit an internal request and receive a typed result, with field/version/request identifiers and timeout/failure handling. Calling `AbstractClient` directly from the engine would break the existing testable state-machine boundary; the existing `OptionRefiner` is an async client wrapper but is not an engine protocol.

suggestions.title: Create separate post-processor configuration instead of reusing plausibility validation
suggestions.rationale: The existing `LLMValidationConfig` describes a batched, submit/review-time plausibility check with `on_error`, `max_fields`, exclusions, and a different verdict shape. `AudioQuestion.llm_validation` and `FormField.llm_validation` already use that vocabulary. Per-answer correction needs its own form/field configuration, explicit typed-family allowlist, threshold, timeout, model, and fail-open behavior; free TEXT and sensitive fields must be rejected by policy before any client call.

suggestions.title: Persist processor provenance through every evidence representation
suggestions.rationale: `AudioAnswer` currently stores transcript, STT confidence, language, recording metadata, and option matching, but no producer field. `_accept` reconstructs the answer and `VoiceEvidenceEnvelope`/`wrap_voice` copy only audio/STT metadata. Add an enum such as `rules`/`llm` to the answer, snapshot, submission envelope, and form-complete evidence, preserving it on confirmation and resume while retaining the existing sensitive transcript masking.

suggestions.title: Define precedence between STT confidence, normalization ambiguity, and LLM confidence
suggestions.rationale: The engine currently confirms free-form speech when STT confidence is below `stt_confirm_threshold`; the Faster Whisper backend supplies `language_probability` as that confidence, and the adapter passes `language=None` for English. The design must specify the outcome matrix for low STT/high LLM, high STT/low LLM, deterministic ambiguity, timeout, and invalid email. Keep the separate STT language/confidence defect out of this feature and do not silently let the new LLM threshold override the existing confirmation policy.

suggestions.title: Clarify phone normalization versus final phone validation
suggestions.rationale: The requested phone normalizer says digits only with no format validation, but the existing submission validator applies `PHONE_PATTERN`, including a minimum length and allowed separators. A normalized short digit string may therefore be accepted by the audio engine and rejected only at submit, while typed phone values follow a different path. Decide whether “no format validation” applies only to normalization or also to submission, then test both paths explicitly.

suggestions.title: Add a layered normalization test matrix and wire-level assertions
suggestions.rationale: Existing tests cover the pure engine flow, lexicon loading, option matching, WebSocket transcription, and voice-envelope round trips, but no tests cover typed-family normalization or processor provenance. Add deterministic unit cases for English and Spanish grammar, engine cases for confirmation/acceptance and typed email rejection, adapter cases for timezone and LLM timeout/stale responses, and submission/snapshot round trips asserting raw transcript masking and `rules`/`llm` provenance.
